# @zakkster/lite-fastbit32 v1.6.1

> Zero-GC, monomorphic 32-bit flag manager for ECS masking, object pools, and 60fps hot-path engine code; FastBit32's bit and mask ops are branchless.

## Overview

FastBit32 wraps a plain 32-bit integer with a fluent, chainable API for bitwise flag operations; its bit and mask ops are branchless. The package also exports `BitMapper` (names <-> bits), seven free iterators, from 1.4.0 `FastBit1024` (a 32 x 32 two-level bitmap that fails closed, so it branches on its checks) and from 1.7.0 `FastBit64` (64 flags in two int32 words, fail-closed). It is an engine primitive designed for performance-critical game loops, ECS architectures, and real-time systems. Zero dependencies. Zero allocations on every hot op. Bundle, 1.7.0 build (REPORTED: one run, 2026-11-10; an `export { ... }` entry through esbuild 0.28.2 --bundle --format=esm --minify | gzip -9 | wc -c): 4784 B whole module (3515 B in 1.6.1), 1064 B FastBit32 alone (1064 B in 1.6.1), 2347 B FastBit1024 alone (2350 B in 1.6.1), 2103 B FastBit64 alone (new in 1.7.0), 1489 B every export except FastBit1024 and FastBit64, VERSION included (1490 B in 1.6.1, where only FastBit1024 is excluded).

**When to use FastBit32:** You need to manage up to 32 boolean flags with maximum performance -- ECS component masks, object pool occupancy, input state, collision layers, render flags, networking packet flags, state machines.

**When NOT to use FastBit32:** You need more than 32 flags (33 to 64: `FastBit64` below, fail-closed; up to 1024: `FastBit1024` below, fail-closed; more: `@zakkster/lite-o1` `BitSet`, fixed capacity [1, 2^25] bits, no clear-bit search), you need BigInt support, or you need strict input validation. FastBit32 is a raw engine primitive -- it trusts the caller.

## Import

```javascript
import { FastBit32, BitMapper, VERSION } from '@zakkster/lite-fastbit32';

// 1.4.0: the 32 x 32 two-level bitmap (pools and id sets up to 1024; fails closed)
import { FastBit1024 } from '@zakkster/lite-fastbit32';

// 1.7.0: 64 flags in two int32 words (fails closed)
import { FastBit64 } from '@zakkster/lite-fastbit32';

// Standalone iteration helpers
import {
    forEachArray, forEachObject, forEachMapped,
    forEachMappedObject, forEachMaskPair, forEachMaskDiff, forEachMaskUnion
} from '@zakkster/lite-fastbit32';

// VERSION is the package version string ('1.6.1'), synced with package.json.
```

## Constructor

```javascript
new FastBit32(initial?: number)
```

- `initial` defaults to `0`.
- Coerced to unsigned 32-bit via `>>> 0`.
- `-1` becomes `4294967295` (all 32 bits set).
- Floats are truncated (`3.9` -> `3`).

## API Reference

All mutating methods return `this` for chaining unless noted otherwise.

### Single Bit Operations

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `.add(bit)` | `this` | Set bit at position 0-31. |
| `.remove(bit)` | `this` | Clear bit at position 0-31. |
| `.toggle(bit)` | `this` | Flip bit at position 0-31. |
| `.has(bit)` | `boolean` | Test if bit is set. |

### Bulk Mask Operations

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `.hasAll(mask)` | `boolean` | True if ALL bits in mask are set. `(~value & mask) === 0` (signedness-agnostic; a mask with bit 31 matches -- FB-01, fixed 1.2.1) |
| `.hasAny(mask)` | `boolean` | True if ANY bit in mask is set. `(value & mask) !== 0` |
| `.hasNone(mask)` | `boolean` | True if NO bits in mask are set. `(value & mask) === 0` |

### In-Place Set Math

| Method | Returns | Operation |
|---|---|---|
| `.clear()` | `this` | Reset to 0. |
| `.union(mask)` | `this` | `value \|= mask` -- add bits. |
| `.difference(mask)` | `this` | `value &= ~mask` -- remove bits. |
| `.intersect(mask)` | `this` | `value &= mask` -- keep only shared bits. |

### Advanced Helpers

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `.count()` | `number` | O(1) popcount (Hamming weight). Active bit count, 0-32. |
| `.countMasked(mask)` | `number` | O(1) popcount within masked region only. |
| `.countRange(start, end)` | `number` | O(1) popcount within INCLUSIVE range `[start, end]` -- FastBit1024 addRange / removeRange are half-open [lo, hi). Caller must ensure `0 <= start <= end <= 31`. |
| `.lowest()` | `number` | Index of least significant set bit (0-31). Returns `-1` if empty. |
| `.highest()` | `number` | Index of most significant set bit (0-31). Returns `-1` if empty. |
| `.nextClearBit()` | `number` | Index of least significant **clear** bit (0-31). Returns `-1` if full. Zero-alloc object-pool slot lookup. |
| `.highestClearBit()` | `number` | Index of most significant **clear** bit (0-31). Returns `-1` if full. |
| `.isEmpty()` | `boolean` | True if value is 0. |
| `.isFull()` | `boolean` | True if all 32 bits are set. |

### Iteration

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `.forEach(callback)` | `this` | O(k) iteration over active bits in ascending order. Callback receives `(bit)`. A callback that captures per-call state allocates per call (FB-11); use the cursor below in a hot loop. |
| `.nextSetBit(from)` | `number` | (1.3.0) Lowest active bit >= `from`, or `-1`. Domain `from` 0..32 (32 -> -1). O(1), branchless, 0 B/op. Cursor: `for (let b = m.nextSetBit(0); b !== -1; b = m.nextSetBit(b + 1))`. |
| `.prevSetBit(from)` | `number` | (1.3.0) Highest active bit <= `from`, or `-1`. Domain `from` -1..31 (-1 -> -1). O(1), branchless. Descending cursor: `b = m.prevSetBit(b - 1)`. |
| `.rank(bit)` | `number` | (1.3.0) Active bits strictly below `bit`. Domain `bit` 0..31 (`rank(31)` on a full word = 31). O(1) SWAR popcount. |

Raw-index ops (`nextSetBit`, `prevSetBit`, `rank`, like `add`/`has`) are NOT validated: outside their domain the answer is unspecified (pinned in test/Pinned.test.mjs until S6).

### Utility

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `.clone()` | `FastBit32` | Independent copy. Mutations do not propagate. Allocates; prefer `.copy()` in a pool. |
| `.copy(other)` | `this` | (1.3.0) `value = other.value`. 0 B/op alternative to `clone()`. |
| `.set(x)` | `this` | (1.3.0) `value = x \| 0` (stored signed int32, like every mutator). |
| `.equals(other)` | `boolean` | (1.3.0) Same set. `(a ^ b) === 0`: signedness-agnostic across ctor-built and mutator-built instances. |
| `.equalsValue(x)` | `boolean` | (1.3.0) Same set as the raw word `x`, signedness-agnostic. `undefined`/`null`/`NaN` behave like 0 (FB-02 class, closed in S6). |
| `.isSubsetOf(mask)` | `boolean` | (1.3.0) Every active bit is in `mask`: `(value & ~mask) === 0`. Dual of `hasAll`. |
| `FastBit32.rangeMask(start, end)` | `number` | (1.3.0) Static, COLD, validated. INCLUSIVE `[start, end]` mask as a signed int32 (the `countRange` pattern) -- FastBit1024 addRange / removeRange are half-open [lo, hi). Throws `RangeError` unless both are integers with `0 <= start <= end <= 31`. |
| `.select(k)` | `number` | (1.5.0) The k-th set bit, 0-based ascending (`select(0) === lowest()`, `select(count() - 1) === highest()`), or `-1` for any int32 `k` outside `0..count()-1` and on an empty set. Inverse of `rank`. O(1) branchless, 0 B/op. Not validated: non-int32 `k` is read as `k \| 0` (pinned until S6). |
| `FastBit32.nextSubset(sub, mask)` | `number` | (1.5.0) Static. `(sub - 1) & mask`, signed int32. From `mask` down: exactly 2^count(mask) submasks, 0 last. `nextSubset(0, mask)` wraps to `mask | 0` (signed). 0 B/op on Node (T6); on a pointer-compressed engine (31-bit Smi) a result outside [-2^30, 2^30) boxes (12 B) through a non-inlined call (FB-12, S7). Not validated. |
| `FastBit32.nextCombination(v)` | `number` | (1.5.0) Static. Next word with the same popcount, strictly greater as uint32 (Gosper), signed int32. Ends at `0` (also `f(0)`, `f(-1)`), never `-1`. 0 B/op on Node (T6); on a pointer-compressed engine (31-bit Smi) a result outside [-2^30, 2^30) boxes (12 B) through a non-inlined call (FB-12, S7). Not validated. |
| `.serialize()` | `number` | Export raw uint32 for JSON/binary storage. |
| `FastBit32.deserialize(n)` | `FastBit32` | Static. Restore from serialized uint32. |

### Debug & Init Helpers

These methods allocate -- keep them out of hot loops.

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `.toBinaryString(padded?)` | `string` | 32-char (or variable) binary string, LSB on the right. Handles the sign bit correctly. Allocates a String. |
| `.toArray()` | `number[]` | Active bit indexes in ascending order. Inlined O(k) scan (no closure allocation). Allocates an Array. |
| `.fromArray(bits)` | `this` | **Replaces** the value with a bitmask built from a bit-index array. Intended for init / deserialization. |

### Property

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `.value` | `number` | The raw 32-bit integer. Safe to read directly in hot paths. |

## BitMapper -- Human-to-Hardware Bridge

Translates semantic string names into bit indices and masks. Keeps engine hot paths fast while letting developers think in words.

```javascript
const mapper = new BitMapper(['Position', 'Velocity', 'Health', 'Magic']);
```

### Constructor

```javascript
new BitMapper(names?: string[])
```

- `names` -- Array of up to 32 flag names. Each name maps to its array index (0-31).
- Throws if more than 32 names are provided.

### BitMapper Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `.get(name)` | `number` | Bit index (0-31) for a flag name. Throws if unknown. |
| `.getMask(names)` | `number` | Combined uint32 mask from an array of flag names. |
| `.getActiveNames(fb32)` | `string[]` | Array of active flag names from a FastBit32 instance. |
| `.getName(bit)` | `string \| undefined` | O(1) reverse lookup -- bit index to string name. |
| `.bit(name)` | `number` | (1.3.0) One-bit mask `1 << get(name)`, signed int32 (bit 31 -> -2147483648). Throws if unknown. |
| `.size` | `number` | (1.3.0) Getter: number of DISTINCT registered names (a duplicate name keeps its last index; FB-06). |

### BitMapper Example

```javascript
const mapper = new BitMapper(['Physics', 'Render', 'AI', 'Input']);
const entity = new FastBit32();
entity.add(mapper.get('Physics')).add(mapper.get('Input'));

mapper.getActiveNames(entity); // ['Physics', 'Input']

const PHYSICS_QUERY = mapper.getMask(['Physics', 'Render']);
entity.hasAll(PHYSICS_QUERY); // false -- missing Render
```

## Standalone Iteration Helpers

All helpers are O(k) where k = number of active bits. No loops over 32 slots -- only active bits are visited.

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `forEachArray` | `(mask, array, cb)` | Active bits -> array indices. `cb(element, bit)` |
| `forEachObject` | `(mask, keys, obj, cb)` | Active bits -> keys array -> object values. `cb(value, key, bit)` |
| `forEachMapped` | `(mask, mapper, cb)` | Active bits -> BitMapper names. `cb(name, bit)` |
| `forEachMappedObject` | `(mask, mapper, obj, cb)` | Active bits -> BitMapper names -> object values. `cb(value, key, bit)` |
| `forEachMaskPair` | `(maskA, maskB, cb)` | Intersection (A & B). `cb(bit)` |
| `forEachMaskDiff` | `(maskA, maskB, cb)` | Difference (A & ~B). `cb(bit)` |
| `forEachMaskUnion` | `(maskA, maskB, cb)` | Union (A \| B). `cb(bit)` |

### Iteration Example

```javascript
const mapper = new BitMapper(['Idle', 'Run', 'Jump', 'Attack']);
const mask = new FastBit32().add(1).add(3); // Run + Attack

forEachMapped(mask, mapper, (name, bit) => {
    console.log(name); // 'Run', then 'Attack'
});
```

## FastBit1024 -- 32 x 32 two-level bitmap (1.4.0)

A fixed-geometry bitmap of up to 1024 bits for slot pools and dense id sets. Storage: `Int32Array(32)` plus two 32-bit summaries (`_active`: word non-empty, `_full`: word all ones) and an exact count, kept by every mutator. No coupling to FastBit32 (tree-shakes alone). 1.6.0 adds save / restore, copy / equals / clone, the three counts, prevSetBit and the range ops.

**Input law: FastBit1024 FAILS CLOSED on every index; FastBit32's hot ops trust the caller (SC-3, open, decided in S6).** An index must be an integer `0 <= i < capacity` (`nextSetBit`: `0 <= from <= capacity`; `prevSetBit`: `-1 <= from <= capacity - 1`). Anything else throws `RangeError` (undefined, null, NaN, 1.5, '3', true, -1 (except prevSetBit's -1), capacity, 2^32, {}); a Symbol, a BigInt or a null-prototype object throws `TypeError` from the index arithmetic. `-0` is slot 0. A rejected call writes nothing; the argument's own conversion (`valueOf` / `toString` / `Symbol.toPrimitive`) still runs once, before the throw. `has(undefined)` throws: it never answers for slot 0. Underscore fields (`_cap`, `_n`, `_active`, `_full`, `_data`) are internal; writing them voids invariants I1-I4. `hasAll`/`hasAny`/`copy`/`equals`/`intersectionSize`/`unionSize`/`differenceSize` check a private-name brand (a private field stamped by the constructor): subclass instances pass; null, a primitive, a FastBit32, a forgery (`Object.create(FastBit1024.prototype)`), a Proxy and a FastBit1024 from a second installed copy of the package throw `TypeError`. Every op is loop-free except forEach/hasAll/hasAny/clear/copy/equals/intersectionSize/unionSize/differenceSize (O(non-empty words)), saveInto/loadFrom (O(image words), and loadFrom rewrites all 32 words; the cold serialize/deserialize reuse them, clone reuses copy) and addRange/removeRange (O(words touched)). Ranges are half-open [lo, hi); FastBit32 countRange / rangeMask are INCLUSIVE [start, end]. Name map to RoaringSet: `hasAny` = `intersects` (no alias); `intersectionSize` / `unionSize` / `differenceSize` share its names.

```javascript
new FastBit1024(capacity?: number)   // integer 1..1024; undefined -> 1024; else RangeError
```

| Member | Returns | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `add(bit)` / `remove(bit)` / `toggle(bit)` | `this` | O(1) | RangeError on a bad index |
| `has(bit)` | `boolean` | O(1) | RangeError on a bad index (the check costs ~0.8 ns, measured) |
| `acquire()` | slot or `-1` | O(1) | the LOWEST free slot; -1 when full |
| `release(slot)` | `this` | O(1) | RangeError on a bad index AND on a free slot (double release) |
| `size` / `capacity` | `number` | O(1) | read-only getters |
| `isEmpty()` / `isFull()` | `boolean` | O(1) | isFull: every bit below capacity set |
| `lowest()` / `highest()` | index or `-1` | O(1) | two `clz32`, no loop |
| `nextClearBit()` | index or `-1` | O(1) | lowest clear bit below capacity |
| `nextSetBit(from)` | index or `-1` | O(1) | from in 0..capacity; capacity -> -1 |
| `prevSetBit(from)` | index or `-1` | O(1), 0 B/op | (1.6.0) highest set bit <= from (inclusive); from in -1..capacity-1, -1 -> -1, else RangeError. Reverse walk: `for (let b = s.prevSetBit(s.capacity - 1); b !== -1; b = s.prevSetBit(b - 1))` |
| `hasAll(other)` / `hasAny(other)` | `boolean` | O(non-empty words of other) | other must be a FastBit1024 (private-name brand), else TypeError (a forgery or a Proxy included); neither method writes to either instance; capacities may differ (exact). `hasAny` is RoaringSet's `intersects` |
| `intersectionSize(other)` / `unionSize(other)` / `differenceSize(other)` | `number` | O(non-empty words), 0 B/op | (1.6.0) count of A AND B / A OR B / A AND NOT B; same brand TypeError; exact for any two capacities (RoaringSet throws RangeError on a universe mismatch; these do not) |
| `copy(other)` / `equals(other)` | `this` / `boolean` | O(non-empty words), 0 B/op | (1.6.0) copy overwrites words and summaries (no rebuild); a differing capacity is accepted only when every set bit of other fits, else RangeError and nothing is written; copy(this) is a no-op. equals is exact across capacities. Same brand TypeError |
| `clone()` | `FastBit1024` | COLD, allocates | (1.6.0) same capacity, same bits |
| `addRange(lo, hi)` / `removeRange(lo, hi)` | `this` | O(words touched), 0 B/op | (1.6.0) set / clear bits lo..hi-1, HALF-OPEN [lo, hi), `0 <= lo <= hi <= capacity` (integers), else RangeError before any write; lo === hi is a no-op. A Symbol or BigInt `lo` throws TypeError; so does such an `hi` when `lo` passes its check |
| `imageLength` | `number` | O(1) | (1.6.0) read-only getter: `1 + ceil(capacity / 32)` (2..33) words |
| `saveInto(out, offset = 0)` | `number` | O(image words), 0 B/op | (1.6.0) writes the image (header `0x46420800 \| capacity`, then data words LSB-first) at out[offset..offset + imageLength); returns offset + imageLength so saves chain. `out` must be a genuine Int32Array or a subclass (intrinsic tag + length), else TypeError; bad offset / no room / detached: RangeError, nothing written |
| `loadFrom(src, offset = 0)` | `number` | O(image words), 0 B/op | (1.6.0) validates the WHOLE image (tag, capacity 1..1024, length, no bit at or above the image capacity, every set bit below THIS capacity) before any write, rebuilds summaries and count (a stored count is never trusted); returns the offset just past the image. Same `src` brand as saveInto; a failure leaves the set unchanged. A SharedArrayBuffer-backed Int32Array is accepted: under a concurrent writer I1-I4 hold, content unspecified |
| `serialize()` / `FastBit1024.deserialize(src, offset = 0)` | `Int32Array` / `FastBit1024` | COLD, allocate | (1.6.0) a fresh image / a new set whose capacity is the image's (throws as loadFrom) |
| `forEach(cb)` | `this` | O(k + non-empty words) | ascending; hoist cb; each word is read once (snapshot): to mutate during the walk use the nextSetBit cursor |
| `clear()` | `this` | O(non-empty words) | |

```javascript
import { FastBit1024 } from '@zakkster/lite-fastbit32';

const slots = new FastBit1024(500);           // slots 0..499
const bullets = new Float64Array(500 * 4);    // x, y, vx, vy per slot

function spawn() {
    const s = slots.acquire();                // lowest free slot, or -1
    if (s === -1) return -1;                  // pool exhausted
    bullets[s * 4] = 0;
    return s;
}
function despawn(s) { slots.release(s); }     // throws on a double release

// closure-free walk over live slots (0 B/op)
for (let s = slots.nextSetBit(0); s !== -1; s = slots.nextSetBit(s + 1)) {
    bullets[s * 4] += bullets[s * 4 + 2];
}
```

Save, load and walk recipes (1.6.0; each snippet was run against `FastBit32.js`):

```javascript
const s = new FastBit1024(500);
s.add(3).add(64).add(499).addRange(100, 104);   // 3, 64, 100..103, 499

// JSON save / load (cold)
const json = JSON.stringify(Array.from(s.serialize()));
const back = FastBit1024.deserialize(new Int32Array(JSON.parse(json)));   // back.equals(s) === true

// Reverse walk, closure-free, 0 B/op: 499, 103, 102, 101, 100, 64, 3
for (let b = s.prevSetBit(s.capacity - 1); b !== -1; b = s.prevSetBit(b - 1)) { /* use b */ }

// Snapshot arena, zero-GC: k sets of the same capacity, chained saveInto offsets
const k = 3, arena = new Int32Array(k * s.imageLength);
let off = 0;
for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) off = s.saveInto(arena, off);   // off === arena.length
off = 0;
for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) off = s.loadFrom(arena, off);   // each call returns the next offset
```

Measured (one full run, node v26.8.2, Apple M4 Pro, witness HOT, net of an empty loop): `acquire()+release()` pair ~3.2 ns, `nextClearBit` ~0.5 ns, `lowest` ~0.34-0.37 ns, `highest` ~0.40-0.47 ns, `has` ~0.91-0.98 ns; each flat across "free (or set) slot in word 0..31". 0 B/op measured in torture T6 for acquire/release, has, nextClearBit, lowest, highest, the nextSetBit cursor and hasAll/hasAny (add/remove/toggle/forEach/clear are not in that lane) and, from 1.6.0, for saveInto, loadFrom, copy, equals, prevSetBit, intersectionSize / unionSize / differenceSize, addRange and removeRange (DETERMINISTIC: an allocation count gated in `npm run torture` on verified-optimized code; serialize / deserialize / clone allocate and have must-fail lanes); perf-gate 0 scavenges at N and 8N for acquire+release.

Measured, 1.5.0 (two fast witness runs, node v26.8.2, Apple M4 Pro, load ~4-5, net ns/op, HOT, flat across density and position): `select` ~3.25-3.35 ns (flatness ratio <= 1.02), `nextSubset` ~0.10-0.21 ns (<= 1.17), `nextCombination` ~0.35-0.43 ns (<= 1.16). `select` is an order of magnitude more than the other constant ops (~3.3 ns vs ~0.1-0.4 ns; a 5-step dependent descent) and still flat. 0 B/op on all three on Node (torture T6 S5 lane, gated < 0.1 B/op). On a pointer-compressed engine (31-bit Smi) the two statics box (12 B) a result outside [-2^30, 2^30) when returned through a non-inlined call (d8 probe; browser measurement in S7, FB-12); `select` returns only -1..31 and stays 0 B/op.

## FastBit64 -- 64 flags, two int32 words (1.7.0)

`FastBit64` holds 64 flags in two signed int32 words: `lo` = bits 0..31, `hi` = bits 32..63, in one object. It is a separate export (no coupling to FastBit32 / FastBit1024). Every op is O(1) and loop-free except `forEach` / `toArray` / `fromArray` (O(k)) and `loadFrom` / `deserialize` (O(image words), at most 33).

```javascript
import { FastBit64 } from '@zakkster/lite-fastbit32';
const entity = new FastBit64().add(3).add(40).add(63);
const sig = new FastBit64().add(3).add(40);
entity.hasAll(sig);        // true
entity.lo; entity.hi;      // 8, -2147483392 (bit 63 set -> hi is negative)
entity.has(64);            // RangeError: fails closed, nothing written
```

Input law (fail closed): every index is an integer 0..63, else `RangeError` (`TypeError` for a Symbol, a BigInt or a null-prototype object); a rejected call writes nothing (the argument's own conversion still runs once before the throw; a conversion that itself throws propagates its own error). Constructor / `setWords` / `equalsWords` words are integers in [-2^31, 2^32), signed or unsigned form, stored `| 0`, else `RangeError`. A method taking another set (`hasAll`, `union`, `equals`, ...) requires a real `FastBit64` (subclasses pass); `{ lo, hi }`, a Proxy, an `Object.create(FastBit64.prototype)` forgery, a FastBit32 or a FastBit1024 throws `TypeError` (V8's own private-brand message). `lo` / `hi` are read-only signed getters.

Members (the shipped surface, FastBit32.d.ts):
- `new FastBit64(lo = 0, hi = 0)`, `lo`, `hi`.
- `add(bit)`, `remove(bit)`, `toggle(bit)` -> this; `has(bit)` -> boolean. `bit` 0..63, else RangeError.
- `hasAll(other)`, `hasAny(other)`, `hasNone(other)`, `isSubsetOf(other)`, `equals(other)` -> boolean; `union(other)`, `difference(other)`, `intersect(other)`, `copy(other)` -> this; `countMasked(other)` -> popcount of `this & other`.
- `setWords(lo, hi)` -> this, `equalsWords(lo, hi)` -> boolean (the two-word form of FastBit32's `set` / `equalsValue`).
- `count()` (0..64), `isEmpty()`, `isFull()`, `clear()`, `lowest()`, `highest()` (-1 when empty), `nextClearBit()`, `highestClearBit()` (-1 when full).
- `nextSetBit(from)` (from 0..64; 64 returns -1), `prevSetBit(from)` (from -1..63, inclusive; -1 returns -1), `rank(bit)` (set bits strictly below `bit`), `select(k)` (k 0..63, RangeError outside; -1 when k >= count()).
- `addRange(lo, hi)`, `removeRange(lo, hi)`, `countRange(lo, hi)`: HALF-OPEN `[lo, hi)`, 0 <= lo <= hi <= 64. FastBit32.countRange(start, end) is INCLUSIVE; FastBit64 follows FastBit1024.
- `forEach(callback)` (O(k), ascending; hoist the callback).
- `imageLength` (3, instance and static), `saveInto(out, offset = 0)`, `loadFrom(src, offset = 0)` -> next offset, `serialize()`, static `deserialize(src, offset = 0)`: the image is `[0x46420840, lo, hi]`, the FastBit1024 image at capacity 64; each class loads the other's (FastBit64.loadFrom takes any FastBit1024-format image whose set bits are all < 64).
- COLD, allocating: `clone()`, `toArray()`, `fromArray(bits)` (every index checked before the single write; overwrites; a detached TypedArray reads as length 0, so the set is cleared, no throw), `toBinaryString(padded = true)` (64 chars, bit 63 first), `serialize()`, `deserialize()`.

Not carried from FastBit32: static `rangeMask` (use `addRange`), static `nextSubset` / `nextCombination`, the number form of `serialize` / `deserialize`, the modulo-32 law and `>>> 0` storage. Not carried from FastBit1024: `acquire` / `release` / `size`. The kernels (popcount / ctz / select) are private module functions, not exports.

64 x 64 = 4096 recipe (1.7.0, a doc recipe, not an export): an `Int32Array(128)` plus two FastBit64 summaries over the 64 slots (`active`: slot non-empty; `full`: slot all ones). Retained bytes: nominal (p8), not yet measured.

```javascript
import { FastBit64 } from '@zakkster/lite-fastbit32';

// 4096 slots = 64 slots of 64 bits. The bits live in one Int32Array(128); two FastBit64
// summaries sit over the 64 slots: `active` (slot has a set bit) and `full` (slot is all ones).
class Bits4096 {
    constructor() { this.words = new Int32Array(128); this.active = new FastBit64(); this.full = new FastBit64(); this.n = 0; }
    static bad(i) { throw new RangeError('Bits4096: index must be an integer 0..4095, got ' + String(i)); }
    has(i) { if ((i & 4095) !== i) Bits4096.bad(i); return (this.words[i >>> 5] & (1 << i)) !== 0; }
    add(i) {
        if ((i & 4095) !== i) Bits4096.bad(i);
        const w = i >>> 5, ws = this.words, old = ws[w], d = old | (1 << i);
        if (d === old) return this;
        ws[w] = d; this.n++;
        const s = i >>> 6;
        this.active.add(s);
        if (~(ws[s << 1] & ws[(s << 1) + 1]) === 0) this.full.add(s);
        return this;
    }
    remove(i) {
        if ((i & 4095) !== i) Bits4096.bad(i);
        const w = i >>> 5, ws = this.words, old = ws[w], d = old & ~(1 << i);
        if (d === old) return this;
        ws[w] = d; this.n--;
        const s = i >>> 6;
        this.full.remove(s);
        if ((ws[s << 1] | ws[(s << 1) + 1]) === 0) this.active.remove(s);
        return this;
    }
    /** Lowest free index, now held; -1 when full. */
    acquire() {
        const s = this.full.nextClearBit();
        if (s === -1) return -1;
        const ws = this.words, lo = ws[s << 1], wi = (s << 1) + ((~lo === 0) ? 1 : 0), c = ~ws[wi];
        const i = (wi << 5) + (31 - Math.clz32(c & -c));
        this.add(i);
        return i;
    }
    /** RangeError on a bad index or a free slot (double release). */
    release(i) {
        if ((i & 4095) !== i) Bits4096.bad(i);
        if ((this.words[i >>> 5] & (1 << i)) === 0) throw new RangeError('Bits4096: release of a free slot ' + i);
        return this.remove(i);
    }
    lowest() {
        const s = this.active.lowest();
        if (s === -1) return -1;
        const ws = this.words, lo = ws[s << 1], wi = (s << 1) + (lo === 0 ? 1 : 0), d = ws[wi];
        return (wi << 5) + (31 - Math.clz32(d & -d));
    }
    /** Lowest set index >= from, or -1; from 0..4096 (4096 ends a walk). */
    nextSetBit(from) {
        if ((from & 8191) !== from || from > 4096) Bits4096.bad(from);
        if (from === 4096) return -1;
        const ws = this.words, s = from >>> 6;
        for (let wi = from >>> 5, m = -1 << from; wi < (s << 1) + 2; wi++, m = -1) {
            const d = ws[wi] & m;
            if (d !== 0) return (wi << 5) + (31 - Math.clz32(d & -d));
        }
        if (s === 63) return -1;
        const t = this.active.nextSetBit(s + 1);
        if (t === -1) return -1;
        const lo = ws[t << 1], wi = (t << 1) + (lo === 0 ? 1 : 0), d = ws[wi];
        return (wi << 5) + (31 - Math.clz32(d & -d));
    }
    get size() { return this.n; }
}

const pool = new Bits4096();
const a = pool.acquire(), b = pool.acquire();   // 0, 1
pool.release(a);                                // a is free again; pool.release(a) twice throws RangeError
pool.acquire();                                 // 0 again: the lowest free slot
```

Names above 32 (1.7.0, a doc recipe): BitMapper is 32 bits. For up to 64 names build the name -> index Map once, resolve a signature when it is created, and keep `hasAll` as the hot check; the Map lookup never runs per frame.

```javascript
import { FastBit64 } from '@zakkster/lite-fastbit32';

const NAMES = ['pos', 'vel', 'acc', 'rot', 'scale', 'sprite', 'anim', 'tint', 'health', 'armor',
    'mana', 'ai', 'target', 'path', 'input', 'camera', 'light', 'shadow', 'audio', 'emitter',
    'trigger', 'collider', 'body', 'joint', 'tag', 'team', 'owner', 'parent', 'child', 'timer',
    'lifetime', 'loot', 'inventory', 'dialog', 'quest', 'score', 'netid', 'replicated', 'dirty', 'dead'];
const BIT = new Map(NAMES.map((n, i) => [n, i]));   // name -> 0..63; built once
function signature(names) {                          // runs when the signature is built, never per frame
    const s = new FastBit64();
    for (const n of names) { const i = BIT.get(n); if (i === undefined) throw new RangeError('unknown name: ' + n); s.add(i); }
    return s;
}
const entity = signature(['pos', 'vel', 'sprite', 'health']), sig = signature(['pos', 'sprite']);
entity.hasAll(sig);   // the hot check: two int32 ANDs, no Map lookup, no allocation
```

GC: 0 B/op on Node (node 26.x; T6 SKIPs below V8 14) in torture T6 (DETERMINISTIC: an allocation count gated in `npm run torture`, verified TurboFan, below 0.1 B/op) on the 24 FastBit64 lanes, inlined and under `--no-turbo-inlining`: has, add+remove, toggle, hasAll, hasAny/hasNone, isSubsetOf/equals, union/diff/intersect, count/countMasked, lowest/highest, nextClearBit/hiClear, nextSetBit walk, prevSetBit walk, rank/select, rank(31)/rank(63), addRange/removeRange, countRange, setWords/equalsWords, lo/hi getters, isEmpty/isFull, clear, forEach (hoisted cb), saveInto, loadFrom, copy. serialize / deserialize / clone / toArray / fromArray / toBinaryString allocate (COLD). Every numeric field starts as a Smi (`#lo = 0; #hi = 0;`, a Hygiene source pin).

Pointer-compressed engines (31-bit Smi: Chrome, Electron): (a) the d8 lane (d8 15.7.37) gates the read, store and mutator (toggle / add / union) windows at <= 2 scavenges per 1e6 ops inlined; the `--no-turbo-inlining` d8 run is REPORTED. The remaining cost: a word outside the 31-bit Smi range (bits 31 and 30 differ) boxes when it crosses a non-inlined call (`setWords` / `equalsWords` arguments, `lo` / `hi` returns, kernel calls when the inlining budget runs out), in Maglev-compiled `loadFrom` (one box per call, nominal), and in interpreter / Sparkplug code; an instance costs about 24 B more than a plain two-field object (two in-place number boxes; nominal). (b) REPORTED, not gated (d8 15.7.37, K = 7, one run, 2026-11-08, Apple M4 Pro (12 cores), quiet host (load1 2.33), node v26.8.2 harness): once a d8 process holds an out-of-Smi instance, mutators on Smi words were measured slower, `toggle` about 1.0 -> about 3.7 ns/op, no allocation either way.

## Critical Caveats

1. **Silent modulo-32 wraparound.** JavaScript bitwise shifts apply `% 32` implicitly. `add(32)` is identical to `add(0)`. `add(40)` is identical to `add(8)`. There is no bounds checking.

2. **Sign bit.** `add(31)` sets the sign bit, so `.value` may read as a negative signed integer in JavaScript. The predicates (`has`, `hasAll`, `hasAny`, `hasNone`, `isEmpty`, `isFull`) are signedness-agnostic: they answer the same for a mask and its `>>> 0` form (FB-01, fixed 1.2.1). To compare two instances use `a.equals(b)` (1.3.0) or `a.equalsValue(x)`; a raw `.value` / `serialize()` comparison needs `(a.value ^ b.value) === 0` or `>>> 0` on both sides. (serialize() itself stays representation-unstable until FB-03 / S6.)

3. **No input validation.** Floats are truncated. Negative bit indices are coerced. NaN becomes 0. FastBit32 trusts the caller for maximum performance.

4. **32-bit limit.** Only bits 0-31 are addressable. Up to 1024 bits: `FastBit1024` (fixed geometry, fails closed). For larger bitfields, use `@zakkster/lite-o1` `BitSet` (fixed capacity, an integer in [1, 2^25] bits; it has no clear-bit search -- no firstClear / nextClear -- so it does not replace the FastBit1024 pool).

## Correct Usage Patterns

### Random pick, submasks, k-of-32 combinations (1.5.0)

```javascript
// Random live flag; -1 on an empty set by itself (count() is 0, select(0) is -1).
const bit = f.select((Math.random() * f.count()) | 0);

// Every submask of m, m down to 0 (2^count(m) of them): visit, then break on 0.
for (let s = m; ; s = FastBit32.nextSubset(s, m)) {
    visit(s);
    if (s === 0) break;
}

// Every k-of-32 set, k >= 1 (C(32, k) words, increasing as unsigned).
for (let v = FastBit32.rangeMask(0, k - 1); v !== 0; v = FastBit32.nextCombination(v)) {
    visit(v);
}
```

### ECS Component Mask Query

```javascript
const POSITION = 0, VELOCITY = 1, SPRITE = 2, COLLISION = 3;
const PHYSICS_QUERY = (1 << POSITION) | (1 << VELOCITY) | (1 << COLLISION);

const entity = new FastBit32();
entity.add(POSITION).add(VELOCITY).add(COLLISION);

if (entity.hasAll(PHYSICS_QUERY)) {
    // Entity matches the physics system query
}
```

### Object Pool -- Find First Free Slot (zero-allocation)

```javascript
const occupied = new FastBit32();

function allocate() {
    const slot = occupied.nextClearBit();   // O(1), zero allocation
    if (slot === -1) return -1;              // Pool full
    occupied.add(slot);
    return slot;
}

function release(slot) {
    occupied.remove(slot);
}

// Bail early when the pool is saturated:
if (occupied.isFull()) return -1;
```

> Prior to v1.2.0 this pattern required `new FastBit32(~occupied.value & 0xFFFFFFFF)` followed by `.lowest()`, which allocated a scratch instance per `allocate()` call. `nextClearBit` is the direct, zero-GC replacement.

### Input State Manager

```javascript
const KEY_LEFT = 0, KEY_RIGHT = 1, KEY_JUMP = 2;
const input = new FastBit32();

// On keydown:
input.add(KEY_JUMP);
// On keyup:
input.remove(KEY_JUMP);
// In game loop:
if (input.has(KEY_JUMP)) jump();
```

### Collision Layer Masks

```javascript
const PLAYER = 0, ENEMY = 1, BULLET = 2, WALL = 3;
const playerCollidesWith = new FastBit32();
playerCollidesWith.add(ENEMY).add(WALL);

if (playerCollidesWith.has(otherEntityLayer)) {
    // Collision detected
}
```

### State Machine

```javascript
const IDLE = 0, RUNNING = 1, JUMPING = 2, ATTACKING = 3;
const state = new FastBit32().add(IDLE);

function startAttack() {
    state.clear().add(ATTACKING);
}
```

### ECS with BitMapper and Iteration

```javascript
const components = new BitMapper(['Position', 'Velocity', 'Sprite', 'AI']);
const entity = new FastBit32();
entity.add(components.get('Position')).add(components.get('AI'));

// Debug: see what's active
console.log(components.getActiveNames(entity)); // ['Position', 'AI']

// Iterate only active components
const systems = { Position: updatePos, Velocity: updateVel, Sprite: draw, AI: think };
forEachMappedObject(entity, components, systems, (system, name, bit) => {
    system(entity); // Only calls updatePos and think
});
```

### Serialization Round-Trip

```javascript
const raw = flags.serialize();       // number (uint32)
const json = JSON.stringify(raw);    // "18" -- not an object
const restored = FastBit32.deserialize(JSON.parse(json));
```

### Chaining

```javascript
const flags = new FastBit32()
    .add(0)
    .add(3)
    .add(7)
    .remove(3)
    .union((1 << 10) | (1 << 12));
```

## Common Mistakes

```javascript
// WRONG: nextCombination ends at 0, never -1 (-1 is the k = 32 combination)
while (v !== -1) v = FastBit32.nextCombination(v); // never ends the way you expect
// RIGHT: loop on v !== 0

// WRONG: nextSubset(0, m) is not a sentinel -- it wraps to m, so this loop never
// ends (and for m = -1 the body never runs at all)
for (let s = m; s !== -1; s = FastBit32.nextSubset(s, m)) visit(s);
// RIGHT: visit, then break on 0 (see the recipe above)

// WRONG: (1 << 32) - 1 is 0, not 32 ones
const all = (1 << 32) - 1;
// RIGHT: FastBit32.rangeMask(0, k - 1)

// WRONG: Bit index out of range -- silently wraps to bit 0
flags.add(32);

// WRONG: Comparing signed vs unsigned after setting bit 31
flags.add(31);
flags.value === 2147483648; // false -- value is -2147483648 (signed)
(flags.value >>> 0) === 2147483648; // true -- correct unsigned comparison

// WRONG: Using FastBit32 for more than 32 flags
// Use @zakkster/lite-o1 BitSet instead (fixed capacity, [1, 2^25] bits; no clear-bit search: no firstClear / nextClear)

// WRONG: Expecting add() to return a boolean
const result = flags.add(5); // returns `this`, not true/false
const check = flags.has(5);  // returns boolean

// WRONG: Mutating and checking in one expression
if (flags.toggle(3).has(3)) { } // Works, but toggle mutates first -- has() checks the NEW state

// WRONG: Assuming clone shares state
const copy = flags.clone();
copy.add(10);
flags.has(10); // false -- clone is independent
```

## Performance Characteristics (FastBit32)

- All single-bit operations: one bitwise instruction, zero branches.
- `count()`: 5 bitwise operations (Hacker's Delight parallel popcount), zero loops.
- `lowest()` / `highest()` / `nextClearBit()` / `highestClearBit()`: 2-5 operations using `31 - Math.clz32(...)` (`highest()` passes `value | 0`, so on Node it never boxes, even after a deopt; pointer-compressed engines: not gated), zero loops, zero branches (`clz32(0)` is 32, so the `-1` sentinel comes for free).
- FastBit1024 is not branchless: it fails closed (a range check and a throw site per index op) and `acquire()` takes the lowest free slot in O(1), about 3.0-3.2 ns per acquire+release pair (numbers above).
- `forEach` and all standalone helpers: O(k) where k = active bits, not 32.
- FastBit32: all methods except `clone()` and `deserialize()` allocate nothing. FastBit1024: `serialize()`, `deserialize()` and `clone()` allocate (COLD); every other member is zero-allocation (DETERMINISTIC T6 gate, on V8 >= 14 (node 26.x), for acquire / release, has, the cursors, hasAll / hasAny and all 1.6.0 hot members; add / remove / toggle / forEach / clear are not in a T6 lane).
- FastBit64: allocates nothing except `serialize()`, `deserialize()`, `clone()`, `toArray()`, `fromArray()` and `toBinaryString()` (COLD); 0 B/op on Node (node 26.x; T6 SKIPs below V8 14) on the 24 T6 lanes listed in the FastBit64 section (DETERMINISTIC), pointer-compressed engines as stated there.
- V8 monomorphic: single hidden class for the lifetime of the object.
